questions.question: Strategic leadership focuses on aligning ____
questions.explanation: Strategic leadership is about setting a long-term vision and then lining up the organisation's resources and capabilities so that vision can actually be achieved. Options A and B describe routine supervision and administration, while D is about formal structure, none of which is the strategic alignment the question describes.

questions.question: In leadership studies, influence is best understood as the leader's capacity to ____
questions.explanation: Influence is the heart of leadership: it is the leader's ability to shape what people think, believe and do, usually without forcing them. Option B describes punishment, and C and D describe control over structures and decisions, which are forms of authority rather than true influence.

questions.question: Leadership development focuses on enhancing ____
questions.explanation: Leadership development aims to grow a person's ability to influence, inspire and work well with others. Option B is too narrow because technical skill alone does not make someone a leader, and A and C are about control systems and formal position rather than personal leadership capability.

questions.question: Power derived from expertise is referred to as ____
questions.explanation: Expert power comes from the special knowledge, skill or experience a person has, which makes others willing to follow their lead. Reward power (A) rests on giving incentives, coercive power (B) on the ability to punish, and legitimate power (C) on holding a formal position.

questions.question: Leadership communication that builds alignment focuses on ____
questions.explanation: Communication builds alignment when people clearly understand the message and see why it matters to them, so clarity and relevance are what count. Sending more information (A) can actually confuse people, and a directive tone (C) or formal language (D) does not by itself create shared understanding.

questions.question: Leadership influence that develops through consistent expertise demonstrates ____
questions.explanation: When people follow a leader because that leader has repeatedly shown real knowledge and skill, the influence is expert power. Referent power (D) is tempting, but it comes from admiration and personal liking, not competence; reward power (A) and legitimate power (B) rest on incentives and formal position.

questions.question: Leadership resilience refers to the capacity to ____
questions.explanation: Resilience is the ability to keep going and adjust when things get hard, bouncing back from pressure and setbacks. Resisting feedback (A), holding on to authority at all costs (B) or avoiding challenges (D) are signs of rigidity or fear, not resilience.

questions.question: Effective leadership decision-making balances ____
questions.explanation: Good leadership decisions combine careful analysis of facts with sound judgement about the situation and people involved. Options B, C and D focus on control, enforcement and speed, which may matter at times but do not describe the balance that makes decisions effective.

questions.question: Leadership legitimacy is strengthened when leaders ____
questions.explanation: Followers accept a leader as legitimate when they see the leader acting fairly and doing the job well. Ignoring follower input (A), using coercion (C) and over-centralising power (D) all weaken legitimacy because they make the leader look unfair or self-serving.

questions.question: Leadership clarity reduces organisational ____
questions.explanation: When a leader is clear about goals, roles and expectations, people know what to do, so ambiguity and confusion go down. Accountability (A), participation (B) and innovation (C) are things clear leadership should increase, not reduce.

questions.question: Leadership development through coaching prioritises ____
questions.explanation: Coaching is a one-to-one development approach built around personalised feedback that helps a person grow. Reinforcing authority (B), watching over tasks (C) and simply giving instructions (D) are control activities, not coaching.

questions.question: Leadership culture within an organisation reflects ____

options.c: Shared norms and values shaped by leaders

questions.explanation: Leadership culture is the set of shared norms and values that leaders shape and that people across the organisation come to live by. Option A is too narrow because culture is shared, not one person's traits; D is wrong because written policies alone do not create culture, and B is an external market factor.

questions.question: Leadership succession planning focuses on ____
questions.explanation: Succession planning means preparing people now so that capable leaders are ready to take over in future. It is not about keeping current structures unchanged (A), handing over authority on the spot (B) or cutting training costs (D); it is a long-term investment in leadership capacity.

questions.question: Leadership influence that endures beyond formal authority is rooted in ____
questions.explanation: Influence that lasts even when the leader has no formal power over people comes from being seen as rightful and trustworthy. Control systems (A), enforcement power (B) and position (D) only work while the formal authority is in place, so they cannot explain influence beyond it.

questions.question: Leadership communication is most effective when it is ____
questions.explanation: Communication works best when the message is clear and has a definite purpose that people can act on. One-way communication (A) shuts out feedback, while complex technical language (C) and excessive formality (D) make messages harder to understand.

questions.question: One defining feature that distinguishes leadership from management is leadership's emphasis on ____
questions.explanation: A common way to separate the two is that leaders set long-term vision and direction, while managers plan, organise and control day-to-day operations. Options A, B and D, hierarchy, rule enforcement and detailed operational control, are features usually linked to management rather than leadership.

questions.question: Leadership assessment often includes evaluation of ____
questions.explanation: Assessing a leader means looking at how they influence people and what results that influence produces. Organisation size (A) says nothing about the leader, compliance alone (B) ignores outcomes and commitment, and popularity (C) is not the same as effectiveness.

questions.question: Situational leadership emphasises adapting leadership style based on ____
questions.explanation: Situational leadership says the best style depends on how ready followers are (their ability and willingness) and on what the task requires. The leader's own personality (B), the size of the organisation (A) and the industry (D) are not the factors this approach uses to choose a style.

questions.question: Leadership influence that depends on offering incentives is associated with ____
questions.explanation: Reward power is the ability to influence people by offering things they value, such as pay rises, praise or promotion. Coercive power (A) works through the threat of punishment, referent power (B) through personal admiration, and expert power (D) through knowledge and skill.

questions.question: A leader who influences subordinates mainly through the threat of punishment, such as queries, demotion or dismissal, is using ____
questions.explanation: Coercive power rests on the ability to punish or withhold things people value, so followers comply out of fear. Reward power (C) is the opposite, working through incentives, referent power (B) rests on admiration of the leader, and expert power (A) on knowledge and skill.

questions.question: Emotional intelligence in leadership primarily supports ____
questions.explanation: Emotional intelligence is the ability to understand and manage your own emotions and those of others, so its main benefit is better relationships and interpersonal effectiveness. Procedural compliance (A), financial accuracy (B) and technical efficiency (C) depend on other skills, not on emotional awareness.

questions.question: Leadership presence is most closely associated with ____
questions.explanation: Leadership presence is the way a leader comes across to others, and it is built mainly on genuine confidence and being authentic. Physical dominance (A) and formal symbols of authority (D) may impress briefly but do not create real presence, and procedural knowledge (C) is a technical skill.

questions.question: Leadership self-regulation primarily supports ____
questions.explanation: Self-regulation means controlling your impulses and emotions so you act calmly and with discipline. It is part of emotional intelligence and has nothing to do with expanding authority (A), dominating others (B) or making followers depend on you (D).

questions.question: Leadership alignment across departments supports ____
questions.explanation: When leaders across departments share the same goals and priorities, units work together and the organisation performs in a coordinated way. Isolation (A), conflict (C) and internal rivalry (D) are exactly the problems that alignment is meant to prevent.

questions.question: Leadership is commonly described as the process through which an individual influences others to achieve ____
questions.explanation: Leadership is widely defined as a process of influencing, guiding and inspiring others towards shared goals. Routine compliance (B) is closer to administration, while personal popularity (C) and social status (D) are personal gains, not the common goals leadership is meant to achieve.

questions.question: Leadership continuity within organisations is strengthened by ____
questions.explanation: Leadership continuity comes from planning succession and developing talent so new leaders are always ready. Holding on to power centrally (B) and rigid control (C) do not prepare successors, and relying on one person's charisma (D) creates a gap when that person leaves.

questions.question: Leadership authority becomes sustainable when it is supported by ____
questions.explanation: Authority lasts when followers trust the leader and accept the leader's right to lead. Coercion (A) and constant supervision (D) produce only short-term compliance, and formal rules alone (C) cannot keep people committed if trust is missing.

questions.question: Legitimate power is primarily based on ____
questions.explanation: Legitimate power comes from the formal position or office a person holds, which gives them the recognised right to make requests. Fear of punishment (A) is coercive power, personal charisma (C) is referent power, and control of rewards (D) is reward power.

questions.question: Leadership effectiveness over time depends on continuous ____
questions.explanation: Because situations, people and environments keep changing, leaders stay effective only by continually learning and adapting. Standardising procedures (A), reinforcing control (B) and consolidating authority (C) do not help a leader respond to change.

questions.question: Vision in leadership serves to ____
questions.explanation: A vision is a picture of where the organisation wants to be, so its role is to give long-term direction. It does not exist to enforce compliance (A), it supports rather than replaces operational planning (B), and it should guide rather than limit strategic flexibility (C).

questions.question: Leadership consistency contributes to ____
questions.explanation: When a leader behaves consistently, people know what to expect, and that predictability builds trust. Consistency does not mean rigidity (A) or resistance to change (D), and it increases rather than reduces accountability (B).

questions.question: Leadership authority that stems from personal attraction and identification is known as ____
questions.explanation: Referent power or authority comes from followers liking, admiring and identifying with the leader as a person. Legitimate authority (A) is based on position, expert authority (C) on knowledge and skill, and coercive authority (D) on the ability to punish.

questions.question: Leadership sustainability over time is reinforced through ____
questions.explanation: Leadership stays strong over time when leaders keep learning and renewing their ideas and skills. Rigid standardisation (A), piling up authority (C) and reducing participation (D) make leadership stale and less able to cope with change.

questions.question: The idea that no single leadership style is universally effective reflects the ____
questions.explanation: The contingency view holds that there is no one best way to lead; the right style depends on the situation. Classical (A), bureaucratic (B) and autocratic (C) thinking tend to assume a single correct way of leading or managing, which is exactly what the contingency view rejects.

questions.question: Leadership is often regarded as a dynamic process because it continuously involves ____

options.a: Ongoing interaction between leaders and followers

questions.explanation: Leadership is called dynamic because it is a relationship that keeps developing through ongoing interaction between leaders and followers. Fixed relationships (B), predetermined outcomes (C) and permanent structures (D) describe something static, which is the opposite of dynamic.

questions.question: Leadership reflection enhances effectiveness by promoting ____
questions.explanation: Reflection makes leaders more effective because it pushes them to examine their own actions, decisions and assumptions honestly. Rigid consistency (A), protecting authority (C) and habitual behaviour (D) are what reflection helps leaders move away from.

questions.question: Leadership influence across cultures requires sensitivity to ____

options.b: The cultural norms and values of the people being led

questions.explanation: Leading across cultures requires sensitivity to the norms and values of each cultural group involved, since what works in one culture may offend in another. Options A, C and D assume that one uniform style of behaviour, communication or authority will work everywhere, which is the mistake cultural sensitivity avoids.

questions.question: Leadership resilience is strengthened through ____
questions.explanation: Leaders become more resilient by learning from difficulties and setbacks and using those lessons next time. Rigidly sticking to plans (A), denying setbacks (C) and avoiding challenges (D) prevent the growth that builds resilience.

questions.question: Leadership inclusiveness involves ____
questions.explanation: Inclusive leadership means actively welcoming and valuing people's different perspectives and backgrounds. Selective participation (A), excluding dissent (B) and demanding conformity (C) are all forms of exclusion.

questions.question: The leadership function of directing involves ____
questions.explanation: Directing is the function of guiding, instructing and motivating subordinates so that plans are carried out. Recruiting members (B) belongs to staffing, while allocating financial resources (C) and evaluating financial performance (D) relate to planning, budgeting and controlling.

questions.question: Leadership credibility is primarily built through ____
questions.explanation: Credibility grows when people see that a leader does what he or she says, again and again. Job titles (A), organisational policies (B) and hierarchical status (D) may give authority, but they do not make people believe and trust the leader.

questions.question: Leadership communication that encourages dialogue is described as ____
questions.explanation: Interactive communication is two-way: the leader shares information and also invites questions, ideas and feedback, which creates dialogue. Directive (A) and coercive (B) communication flow one way from the top, and transactional (C) refers to exchanging rewards for performance.

questions.question: Leadership learning from failure emphasises ____
questions.explanation: Learning from failure means reflecting on what went wrong and using that insight to improve. Avoiding risk (B), punishing people (C) and blaming others (D) discourage honest reflection and stop real learning.

questions.question: Leadership accountability requires leaders to ____
questions.explanation: Accountability means leaders take responsibility for the results of their decisions and actions, whether good or bad. Avoiding delegation (A), limiting transparency (B) and putting personal authority first (D) all work against being answerable to others.

questions.question: Leadership effectiveness in teams depends heavily on ____
questions.explanation: Teams perform well when each member knows their role and the leader coordinates everyone's effort towards the common goal. Minimal interaction (A) and individual competition (C) break teamwork apart, and strict supervision (B) controls people without building coordination.

questions.question: Leadership influence across virtual teams relies heavily on ____
questions.explanation: In virtual teams the leader cannot rely on being physically present, so clear communication and mutual trust become the main tools of influence. Physical presence (C), informal observation (A) and close hierarchical supervision (B) are hard or impossible when people work remotely.

questions.question: Leadership commitment from followers is strongest when leaders create ____
questions.explanation: Followers are most committed when they understand and believe in the meaning and purpose of their work. Fear of sanctions (B) and strict monitoring (C) produce compliance rather than commitment, and incentives alone (D) keep people only as long as the rewards last.

questions.question: Leadership effectiveness across levels depends on ____
questions.explanation: Leaders at different levels face different people, tasks and pressures, so they need contextual awareness to adjust their approach. A uniform style (D), rigid hierarchy (B) and removing autonomy (A) ignore context and reduce effectiveness.

questions.question: Leadership development initiatives primarily aim to build ____
questions.explanation: Leadership development aims to build real competence and the flexibility to behave in the way each situation needs. Procedural knowledge alone (A) is too narrow, and hierarchy (C) and positional authority (D) come from structure, not from development.

questions.question: Leadership decision legitimacy increases when followers perceive decisions as ____
questions.explanation: People accept decisions more readily when they see them as fair and based on sound reasoning. Arbitrary (B), opaque or secretive (C) and leader-centred (D) decisions make followers suspicious and reduce legitimacy.

questions.question: Leadership effectiveness is enhanced when leaders demonstrate ____
questions.explanation: Self-aware leaders understand their own strengths, weaknesses and emotions, and reflection helps them improve over time. Rigid consistency (B), unilateral control (C) and emotional detachment (D) make leaders less responsive to people and situations.

questions.question: Leadership stability is enhanced when organisational values are ____
questions.explanation: Values provide stability when leaders state them clearly and actually live by them every day. Values that are ignored (A), imposed without discussion (B) or applied inconsistently (C) create cynicism and confusion instead of stability.

questions.question: Leadership role modelling affects followers primarily through ____
questions.explanation: Role modelling works because followers watch what leaders do and copy that example. Positional authority (A), formal instruction (C) and policy enforcement (D) tell people what to do, but role modelling influences them by showing.

questions.question: Leadership adaptability becomes critical in environments characterised by ____
questions.explanation: Adaptability matters most when the environment changes quickly and the future is uncertain, because yesterday's approach may no longer work. Strict regulation (A), predictable demand (B) and routine stability (D) describe settings where established methods usually still work.

questions.question: Leadership influence through rewards primarily appeals to ____
questions.explanation: Rewards such as pay, bonuses and promotion are external incentives, so they appeal to extrinsic motivation. Intrinsic motivation (C) comes from enjoying or valuing the work itself, while moral obligation (A) and emotional attachment (D) are internal reasons for acting.

questions.question: The concept that leadership is not confined to formal authority positions highlights leadership as a ____
questions.explanation: If anyone can lead without holding a formal post, then leadership is really a process of social influence among people. Hierarchical entitlement (A), bureaucratic obligation (B) and procedural responsibility (C) all tie leadership to positions or rules.

questions.question: A central assumption in modern leadership thought is that leadership can be ____
questions.explanation: Modern leadership thinking assumes leaders are not only born but can be made, so leadership can be learned and developed. It is not inherited through years of service (A), not limited to senior executives (B) and not something rules can enforce (D).

questions.question: Leadership motivation is strengthened when leaders ____
questions.explanation: People are more motivated when their tasks connect with what they personally value and find meaningful. Discouraging autonomy (A), giving little feedback (C) and relying only on authority (D) all reduce motivation.

questions.question: Leadership judgement is best described as the ability to ____
questions.explanation: Good judgement means combining past experience with a clear reading of the current situation to choose the right course of action. Applying rules mechanically (B) ignores the situation, and avoiding uncertainty (A) or delegating every decision (D) is avoiding judgement altogether.

questions.question: Leadership learning is most effective when it is ____
questions.explanation: Leaders learn best by doing and then reflecting on what happened, which is experiential and reflective learning. Limiting learning to formal training (B), keeping it purely theoretical (C) or separating it from practice (D) cuts it off from real experience.

questions.question: Leadership direction becomes clearer when goals are ____
questions.explanation: Direction is clear when goals are specific and understood and shared by everyone involved. Vague goals (A), constantly changing goals (B) and goals imposed without explanation (D) leave people unsure what they are working towards.

questions.question: The primary role of leadership in change management is to ____
questions.explanation: During change, people need to understand why it is happening and where it is heading, so the leader's main role is to communicate purpose and direction. Rules (A), fast enforcement (B) and centralised control (C) may force compliance but do not win support for change.

questions.question: Leadership adaptability refers to the leader's ability to ____
questions.explanation: Adaptability is the ability to change one's behaviour to suit the situation, the people and the task at hand. Avoiding decisions (A), rigid consistency (B) and delegating everything (C) are not adapting at all.

questions.question: Behavioural leadership theories primarily examine what leaders ____
questions.explanation: Behavioural theories shifted attention from who leaders are to what they actually do, such as how they handle tasks and relate to people. Traits leaders are born with (B) are the focus of trait theories, while inherited status (C) and inner beliefs (D) are not what behavioural theories measure.

questions.question: Leadership credibility is undermined when leaders ____
questions.explanation: Credibility collapses when a leader's actions do not match the values he or she preaches, because people stop believing what the leader says. Open communication (B), accepting responsibility (C) and encouraging participation (D) all build credibility rather than undermine it.

questions.question: Leadership trustworthiness is reinforced when leaders consistently ____
questions.explanation: People trust leaders who keep their promises consistently. Avoiding hard decisions (A), restricting information (B) and putting self-interest first (D) all signal that the leader cannot be relied upon.

questions.question: Path-goal theory identifies directive, supportive, participative and __________________ leadership styles.
questions.explanation: Path-goal theory says leaders help followers reach goals by choosing among four styles: directive, supportive, participative and achievement-oriented. Options A, C and D are not part of this theory; autocratic and bureaucratic are separate traditional styles.

questions.question: Leadership requires the capacity to __________________ others.
questions.explanation: Leadership is commonly defined as a process of influencing, guiding and inspiring others towards shared goals. Options B, C and D describe pushing people aside, which is not leadership.

questions.question: A core element in most leadership definitions is the ability to __________________
questions.explanation: Most definitions describe leadership as the process of influencing people's behaviour towards shared goals. Option D is tempting, but enforcing compliance relies on formal authority, which is closer to management or command; A and B are not the core of leadership.

questions.question: Setting goals, clarifying roles and aligning group efforts toward shared outcomes are all part of which core component of leadership?
questions.explanation: Providing direction means setting a clear vision, defining goals, clarifying roles and aligning everyone's efforts toward shared outcomes. Option A (managing change and conflict) deals with guiding people through transitions and disagreements, while Option D (motivating followers) is about inspiring commitment rather than setting the course.

questions.question: When a leader inspires followers through a compelling picture of the future, this reflects the quality of __________________
questions.explanation: Vision is a leader's ability to picture a desirable future and inspire people to work towards it. Options A, B and D are routine management tasks that keep things running but do not inspire.

questions.question: A leader who evaluates outcomes honestly and admits mistakes when necessary is displaying which characteristic of an effective leader?
questions.explanation: Accountability and responsibility means leaders own their decisions, judge results honestly and admit mistakes, which builds public confidence. Option A (emotional intelligence) is about managing emotions and empathy, and Option C (vision and strategic thinking) is about anticipating the future rather than reviewing past outcomes.

questions.question: Hersey and Blanchard's Situational Leadership Theory emphasises adapting leadership style to the followers':
questions.explanation: In Hersey and Blanchard's model, the leader chooses a style (telling, selling, participating or delegating) according to how able and willing followers are to perform a task, which is called their maturity or readiness. Culture, emotional stability and intelligence (options C, A and D) may matter in real life, but they are not the variable the model uses to choose a style.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST defines leadership in an organisational context?

options.a: The process of influencing others to achieve a common goal
options.b: The management of organisational resources for profit
options.c: The capacity to delegate tasks to subordinates efficiently
options.d: The ability to command obedience through positional authority

questions.explanation: Leadership is a process of influencing, guiding and inspiring people toward shared goals, and it works through trust and commitment rather than position alone. Option D describes the use of formal authority, which can exist without real leadership, while delegation (option C) and managing assets for profit (option B) are management activities rather than definitions of leadership.

questions.question: The Trait Theory of leadership argues that leaders are:

options.b: Made through training and environmental conditioning
options.c: Defined by the situation they find themselves in
options.d: Born with inherent personal attributes that distinguish them

questions.explanation: Trait Theory, which grew out of the 'great man' view, holds that effective leaders possess inborn qualities such as intelligence, confidence and determination that set them apart from non-leaders. Option B reflects the behavioural view that leadership can be learned, and option C reflects situational or contingency thinking, while option A is about how leaders are selected, not what makes them leaders.

questions.question: Contingency theories of leadership suggest that leadership effectiveness depends on:

options.a: A fixed set of universal leadership traits
options.b: The moral character of the leader alone
options.c: The number of followers a leader controls
options.d: The match between leadership style and situational factors

questions.explanation: Contingency theories, such as Fiedler's model, argue that no single style works everywhere: a leader is effective when his or her style fits the situation, including the task, the followers and the leader's position power. Option A is the trait view that contingency theories reject, and options B and C ignore the situation entirely.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically considered a characteristic of an effective leader?
questions.explanation: Effective leaders influence people through vision, integrity, good communication and emotional intelligence, and they listen to others rather than force their opinions on them. Imposing personal views reduces participation, creativity and trust. Options C, A and B are all commonly listed qualities of effective leaders.

questions.question: The Behavioural Theory of leadership differs from the Trait Theory in that it focuses on:

options.a: The situational demands placed on leaders
options.d: What leaders actually do rather than their innate qualities

questions.explanation: Behavioural theories, such as the Ohio State and Michigan studies, shifted attention from who leaders are to how they behave, for example how much they focus on tasks or on people. This implies that leadership can be learned. Option B describes Trait Theory itself, and option A describes situational or contingency theories.

questions.question: Which leadership function primarily involves inspiring followers to work willingly toward a shared vision?
questions.explanation: Motivating and inspiring followers goes beyond giving instructions: it involves communicating meaningful goals, recognising achievements and building commitment so that people contribute willingly. Controlling (option D) checks performance against standards, organising (option A) arranges tasks and structures, and budgeting (option C) allocates money, none of which is mainly about inspiration.

questions.question: Path-Goal Theory, developed by Robert House, proposes that a leader's primary role is to:

options.b: Prioritise organisational structure over human relations
options.d: Clarify paths to goals and remove obstacles for followers

questions.explanation: Path-Goal Theory says leaders motivate followers by making the route to goals clear, removing obstacles and providing the support or direction followers need, choosing among directive, supportive, participative and achievement-oriented behaviours. Option A sounds close because rewards matter in the theory, but consistent reward and punishment is the core of transactional leadership, not the main idea of Path-Goal Theory.

questions.question: The concept of 'leadership role' is BEST described as:

options.a: The remuneration package attached to a leadership position
options.b: A fixed job description assigned by HR
options.c: The behaviours expected of a leader within an organisational or social context
options.d: The legal authority granted to a public official

questions.explanation: A leadership role is the set of behaviours people expect from a leader in a given setting, such as giving direction, motivating others, making decisions and setting ethical standards. A job description (option B) is a formal document, legal authority (option D) is a basis of power, and pay (option A) is a reward attached to a position, so none captures what a role means.

questions.question: A commonly cited limitation of the Trait Theory of leadership is that:

options.a: It assumes leadership can be learned through training
options.b: Researchers have not agreed on a consistent set of traits that guarantees effective leadership
options.c: It ignores the personal qualities of leaders
options.d: It focuses too heavily on situational factors

questions.explanation: Decades of trait research produced long and inconsistent lists of qualities, and people with the 'right' traits do not always lead well, so the theory cannot reliably predict who will be effective. It also ignores the situation and the followers. Option D is the opposite of the theory's weakness, option C is false because traits are its whole focus, and option A is the behavioural view.

questions.question: A major limitation of the Behavioural Theory of leadership is that it:

options.a: Assumes that leaders are born, not made
options.b: Focuses only on followers' maturity levels
options.d: Has not identified a single style of behaviour that is effective in every situation

questions.explanation: Behavioural studies classified leaders by what they do, such as task-oriented or people-oriented behaviour, but they could not show that any one style works best everywhere, because they paid little attention to the situation. Option A is a criticism of Trait Theory, option C contradicts the theory's focus on behaviour, and option B describes Hersey and Blanchard's situational model.

questions.question: Which leadership function involves setting a clear vision, defining objectives and clarifying roles and responsibilities for followers?
questions.explanation: Providing direction means establishing a vision, setting achievable objectives, clarifying who does what and aligning group effort toward shared outcomes; without it, institutions suffer confusion and conflict. Managing change and conflict (option B) deals with transitions and disagreements, maintaining ethical standards (option D) with integrity, and motivating followers (option C) with building commitment.

questions.question: Contemporary governance and management studies describe leadership as a 'relational process'. What does this mean?

options.a: Leadership is the formal authority attached to a job title or office
options.b: Leadership emerges through interaction between leaders and followers in a specific context
options.c: Leadership is a fixed relationship in which followers simply obey the leader
options.d: Leadership is a personal quality carried by one person regardless of followers

questions.explanation: Seeing leadership as relational means it is not a one-person activity: it grows out of the interaction between leaders and followers within an organisational, social or political setting. Option D treats leadership as something one person holds alone, and option A reduces it to position, which is exactly the one-person view the relational idea rejects. Option C makes followers passive, which also misses the two-way interaction.

questions.question: Effective leadership is said to depend on four things. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: Effective leadership rests on trust, communication, legitimacy and shared commitment to common objectives, all of which are built through the leader-follower relationship. Inherited social status is not part of that list; a person can inherit a title and still fail to lead. Options B, A and C are all on the list.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the core components of leadership?

options.d: Preparing the organisation's statutory financial statements

questions.explanation: The core components of leadership are providing direction, motivating followers, making decisions, maintaining ethical standards, and managing change and conflict. Preparing statutory financial statements is an accounting task, not a component of leadership. Options A, B and C are all core components.

questions.question: The new managing director of a Lagos logistics firm announces a five-year vision, sets achievable quarterly objectives, clarifies who is responsible for what, and aligns all departments behind the same targets. Which core component of leadership is she mainly demonstrating?
questions.explanation: Providing direction means setting a vision, setting achievable objectives, clarifying roles and responsibilities, and aligning group efforts toward shared outcomes, which is exactly what she is doing. Option A is about guiding people through transitions and disagreements, and option D is about integrity and fairness. Option C is about building morale and commitment, which is related but not the focus here.

questions.question: When an organisation or governance system lacks clear direction from its leaders, what does it often experience?
questions.explanation: Without a clear vision and priorities, people pull in different directions, so organisations often experience confusion, inefficiency and conflict. Options B, C and D are all positive outcomes that come from good leadership, not from its absence.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way effective leaders motivate followers?

options.d: Relying only on issuing instructions to get work done

questions.explanation: Motivation goes beyond issuing instructions; it involves encouraging commitment, building morale and giving people a sense of purpose. Leaders do this by recognising achievements, communicating meaningful goals, creating a supportive environment, showing empathy and fairness, and building trust. Options C, A and B are all genuine ways of motivating followers.

questions.question: Good leadership decision-making requires all of the following EXCEPT:

options.b: Choosing the first available option to save time

questions.explanation: Good decisions need critical thinking and analysis, consultation with stakeholders, evaluation of alternatives, risk assessment and accountability for outcomes. Grabbing the first available option skips the evaluation of alternatives altogether. Options C, D and A are all requirements of good decision-making.

questions.question: After a new state policy on market levies sparks protests by traders, the commissioner holds town-hall meetings, explains the transition clearly, listens to traders' concerns and negotiates a phased compromise. Which core component of leadership is this?
questions.explanation: Managing change and conflict involves communicating clearly during transitions, encouraging dialogue, addressing resistance and concerns, negotiating solutions and keeping stability, which matches the commissioner's actions. Option A is about setting vision and objectives in the first place, and option C is about integrity and fairness. Option D is part of the process, but the situation is mainly about handling resistance to a change.

questions.question: In governance contexts, effective conflict management by leaders mainly helps to:

options.a: Prevent social unrest and promote inclusive decision-making
options.b: Remove the need for consultation with citizens
options.c: Guarantee that every policy is popular
options.d: Concentrate decision power in the leader's hands

questions.explanation: When leaders handle disagreement constructively, they prevent social unrest and make decision-making more inclusive. Option D describes centralisation, which often worsens conflict, and option B is the opposite of inclusive decision-making. Option C overstates what any leader can achieve.

questions.question: Maintaining ethical standards as a leader involves all of the following EXCEPT:

options.b: Keeping decisions hidden from those affected by them

questions.explanation: Ethical leadership involves promoting transparency and accountability, upholding fairness and justice, avoiding corruption and abuse of power, respecting diversity and human rights, and using resources responsibly. Hiding decisions from those affected is the opposite of transparency. Options A, D and C are all part of maintaining ethical standards.

questions.question: As a characteristic of effective leaders, emotional intelligence refers to the ability to:

options.a: Use followers' emotions to secure obedience
options.b: Understand and manage one's own emotions while recognising the feelings of others
options.c: Hide all emotions so that followers cannot read the leader
options.d: Think logically without being affected by people's feelings

questions.explanation: Emotional intelligence is the ability to understand and manage your own emotions while recognising how others feel, which helps leaders handle stress, resolve conflict and show empathy. Option C confuses emotional control with concealment, and option A describes manipulation. Option D ignores the 'others' side of emotional intelligence entirely.

questions.question: Before investing N500 million in a new product line, the CEO of an Ibadan manufacturing firm studies emerging market trends, anticipates risks over the next decade and aligns company resources with long-term goals. Which characteristic of an effective leader does this show?
questions.explanation: Vision and strategic thinking is the ability to foresee future opportunities and challenges and develop strategies for them: setting long-term goals, anticipating risks, identifying trends and aligning resources. Option A concerns managing emotions and empathy, and option D concerns sharing ideas and listening. Option C is about owning the results of decisions afterwards.

questions.question: Integrity is described as the foundation of a leader's:
questions.explanation: Integrity, meaning honesty, transparency and fairness, is the foundation of leadership credibility because it makes followers and stakeholders trust the leader. Option D comes from position rather than character, and option B can be won without integrity. Option A has nothing to do with integrity.

questions.question: Ethical failures in leadership often result in:
questions.explanation: When leaders are corrupt or dishonest, trust collapses and institutions stop working, so ethical failures often lead to governance crises and institutional breakdown. Options D, B and A are benefits of good leadership, not consequences of ethical failure.

questions.question: In governance systems, a leader's adaptability and innovation mainly support:
questions.explanation: Adaptable leaders embrace new ideas, adjust strategies to changing conditions and encourage creative problem-solving, which helps institutions bounce back from shocks, that is, institutional resilience. Options B and D are what happens when leaders fail to adapt. Option C is an effect of weak institutions.

questions.question: After the university's new online course-registration portal crashes, the registrar publicly admits the rollout was poorly planned, accepts responsibility and orders an honest review of what went wrong. Which characteristic of effective leaders is he displaying?
questions.explanation: Responsible leaders accept responsibility for their decisions, evaluate outcomes honestly, admit mistakes and stay transparent, which is exactly the registrar's response. Option A is about planning for the future, and option C is about embracing new ideas. Option B concerns managing emotions and empathy rather than owning a failure.

questions.question: Effective communication by a leader mainly helps to:

options.b: Reduce the need for feedback from followers
options.c: Replace the need for clear decisions
options.d: Keep information within the top management

questions.explanation: Strong leaders communicate clearly, listen actively, encourage open dialogue and manage information responsibly, and this builds cooperation and cuts down misunderstandings. Option B is wrong because good communicators actively seek feedback, and option D contradicts open dialogue. Option C is wrong because communication supports decisions but does not replace them.

questions.question: Leaders with high emotional intelligence typically do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.d: React to stress by shifting blame onto subordinates

questions.explanation: Emotionally intelligent leaders handle stress well, resolve conflicts constructively, show empathy and build strong relationships. Blaming subordinates under pressure shows poor emotional control. Options A, C and B all describe high emotional intelligence.

questions.question: In leadership and governance, the situation in which leaders use their authority for personal gain rather than for public or organisational benefit is called:
questions.explanation: Corruption happens when leaders use their authority for personal gain instead of the public good, for example through bribery, embezzlement, nepotism or abuse of resources. Option B is when outside actors push decisions for partisan interests, and option C is when organisations lack structures or capacity. Option A is usually a result of corruption, not its definition.

questions.question: A senator repeatedly pressures the head of a federal agency to award jobs and contracts to party loyalists rather than to qualified applicants. Which leadership challenge in governance does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Political interference is when outside actors influence a leader's decisions for personal or partisan interests rather than the common good, which is what the senator is doing. Option B is about secrecy in decision-making, and option A is about a lack of structures or capacity. Option D may follow from such interference but is not the challenge described.

questions.question: Which leadership response is most directly recommended for dealing with political interference?

options.b: Centralising all decisions in one office
options.d: Reducing professional standards to avoid conflict

questions.explanation: Leaders respond to political interference by upholding professional ethics, strengthening institutional safeguards and promoting merit-based decisions, so that choices rest on qualification rather than loyalty. Option C makes interference easier, and option D is actually a consequence of interference. Option B does not protect decisions from outside pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following is an effect of weak institutions in governance?
questions.explanation: When organisations lack effective structures, capacity or independence, the effects include inefficient service delivery, poor regulatory enforcement and leaders relying on informal networks to get things done. Options D and B are the opposite of those effects. Option C is not an effect of weak institutions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of low citizen trust in leaders?
questions.explanation: Low citizen trust is caused by corruption scandals, poor service delivery and lack of accountability. Delivering tangible results is one of the leadership responses that rebuilds trust, not a cause of losing it. Options C, B and D are the listed causes.

questions.question: A local government council is accused of hiding how it spends its N2 billion annual budget. Which leadership response best addresses this lack of transparency?

options.a: Setting up public reporting systems on spending
options.b: Reducing the number of public consultations
options.c: Keeping budget details with the chairman only
options.d: Restricting journalists' access to council records

questions.explanation: Responses to a lack of transparency include open communication channels, public reporting systems and inclusive policy discussions, all of which let citizens see how money is used. Options D, B and C all increase secrecy and would make the problem worse.

questions.question: Leadership is particularly important in governance because leaders:

options.a: Remove the need for followers to participate
options.b: Shape institutional direction, set ethical standards and manage competing interests
options.c: Replace laws and institutions with personal authority
options.d: Guarantee that citizens never disagree with policy

questions.explanation: Leaders matter in governance because they shape institutional direction, establish ethical standards, coordinate collective action and manage competing interests. Option A contradicts the idea that followers are partners, and option C describes personal rule rather than good governance. Option D is unrealistic.

questions.question: In governance, the quality of leadership most directly determines which of the following?

options.a: Policy direction, institutional performance and citizens' trust in institutions
options.b: Only the size of the civil service
options.c: Only the personal wealth of the leader
options.d: Only the number of political parties

questions.explanation: In governance, leadership determines policy direction, how well institutions perform, and how much citizens trust public institutions. Options C, B and D each pick a narrow factor that leadership quality does not mainly decide.

questions.question: The 'Great Man' theory of leadership is most closely linked to which approach?
questions.explanation: The Great Man theory holds that great leaders are born with special qualities, which is the starting point of the trait approach. Option B studies what leaders do rather than who they are, and option D argues that effectiveness depends on the situation. Option C is about reward-based exchange.

questions.question: A major criticism of the trait approach to leadership is that it:

options.a: Focuses too heavily on the needs of followers
options.b: Assumes leadership style must change with every task
options.c: Relies on rewards and punishments to explain behaviour
options.d: Has not produced a consistent list of traits and ignores the situation

questions.explanation: Researchers who reviewed trait studies found no consistent set of traits that always separates leaders from non-leaders, and the approach ignores the situation in which leadership happens. Option A fits servant leadership more than trait theory, and option C describes transactional leadership. Option B is a contingency idea.

questions.question: The Ohio State leadership studies identified two dimensions of leader behaviour. What were they?

options.a: Contingent reward and management by exception
options.b: Concern for production and concern for people

questions.explanation: The Ohio State studies described leader behaviour in terms of initiating structure (organising tasks and roles) and consideration (concern for subordinates' welfare and respect). Option B is the language of the Blake and Mouton Managerial Grid, and option D names factors in Fiedler's contingency model. Option A lists elements of transactional leadership.

questions.question: A supervisor at a bottling plant in Ikeja is known for being friendly, respecting his workers' ideas and showing real concern for their welfare. In the Ohio State studies, this behaviour is called:
questions.explanation: Consideration describes leader behaviour that shows trust, respect and concern for followers' welfare, which matches this supervisor. Option A is the task side, such as assigning work and setting standards. Option C is a transactional practice of intervening when things go wrong, and option B is a Fiedler situational factor.

questions.question: The University of Michigan leadership studies classified leaders as either:

options.d: Task-motivated or relationship-motivated on the LPC scale

questions.explanation: The Michigan studies contrasted employee-centred leaders, who focus on people and their needs, with job-centred (production-centred) leaders, who focus on tasks and output. Option B reflects the Iowa studies by Kurt Lewin, and option A is a later contemporary distinction. Option D is Fiedler's contingency model.

questions.question: On the Blake and Mouton Managerial Grid, a manager rated 9,9 (high concern for people and high concern for production) practises:
questions.explanation: The 9,9 position combines maximum concern for production with maximum concern for people and is called team management, usually presented as the ideal. Option D is 1,9 (people high, production low), option A is 1,1 (both low), and option C is 5,5 (moderate on both).

questions.question: A branch manager keeps his staff happy with relaxed rules, frequent parties and little pressure, but the branch rarely meets its targets. On the Managerial Grid, his style is best described as:
questions.explanation: Country club management (1,9) shows high concern for people but low concern for production, creating a comfortable atmosphere while output suffers. Option D is high on both, and option B is high on production with little concern for people. Option C shows little concern for either people or production, but this manager clearly cares about staff comfort.

questions.question: Kurt Lewin's leadership studies at the University of Iowa identified which three leadership styles?
questions.explanation: Lewin's Iowa studies compared groups led in autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire ways, and these became the classic traditional styles. Option A lists styles from Hersey and Blanchard's situational model, and option B comes from House's path-goal theory. Option D mixes later contemporary approaches.

questions.question: In Fiedler's contingency model, the Least Preferred Co-worker (LPC) scale is used to determine:

options.a: Whether a leader is task-oriented or relationship-oriented
options.c: How much position power the leader holds
options.d: How mature or ready the followers are

questions.explanation: Fiedler used the LPC scale to identify a leader's basic style: a leader who describes their least preferred co-worker harshly is task-oriented, while one who describes them favourably is relationship-oriented. Option D is the focus of Hersey and Blanchard's model, and option C is one of Fiedler's situational factors, not what the LPC measures. Option B relates to transactional exchange.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three factors Fiedler used to judge how favourable a situation is for a leader?
questions.explanation: Fiedler judged situational favourableness by leader-member relations, task structure and position power. Follower maturity or readiness belongs to Hersey and Blanchard's situational leadership model, not Fiedler's. Options A, D and B are Fiedler's three factors.

questions.question: Because Fiedler assumed that a leader's style is relatively fixed, his model suggests that organisations should:

options.a: Train every leader to switch styles daily
options.b: Allow followers to choose their leader's style
options.c: Ignore the situation and select leaders by traits
options.d: Match leaders to suitable situations or change the situation

questions.explanation: Since Fiedler believed leaders cannot easily change their basic style, the practical advice is to place leaders in situations that suit them, or to change the situation to fit the leader. Option A reflects situational models such as Hersey and Blanchard's, which assume flexibility. Option C returns to trait thinking, and option B is not part of the model.

questions.question: A fresh graduate trainee in a Port Harcourt oil-services firm is unable to perform a new technical task and is unsure of himself. Under Hersey and Blanchard's situational model, which style should his supervisor use?
questions.explanation: Followers with low readiness, who lack both ability and confidence, need the telling style: clear, specific instructions and close supervision. Option D suits followers who are willing but still lack ability. Option C suits able but unsure followers, and option A suits followers who are both able and willing.

questions.question: A senior accountant is highly skilled, confident and keen to take ownership of the month-end close. Under Hersey and Blanchard's situational model, the most suitable style is:
questions.explanation: Followers with high readiness, who are both able and willing, respond best to delegating, where the leader hands over responsibility with little direction or support. Options A and D give heavy direction that would frustrate a capable follower. Option B still combines high direction with high support, which this accountant does not need.

questions.question: In Hersey and Blanchard's situational model, the 'selling' (coaching) style combines:

options.a: Low task behaviour and high relationship behaviour
options.b: High task behaviour and high relationship behaviour
options.c: Low task behaviour and low relationship behaviour
options.d: High task behaviour and low relationship behaviour

questions.explanation: Selling keeps giving direction (high task) while also explaining decisions and offering support (high relationship). Option D is telling, option A is participating, and option C is delegating.

questions.question: Which of the following is a contingency theory of leadership?
questions.explanation: Fiedler's model is the classic contingency theory because it says effectiveness depends on matching the leader's style to the favourableness of the situation. Option B is a trait theory. Options A and C are behavioural approaches that describe what leaders do without making the situation central.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to the behavioural approach to leadership?
questions.explanation: The Managerial Grid describes leader behaviour in terms of concern for people and concern for production, which makes it a behavioural approach. Options D and A are contingency or situational theories because they tie effectiveness to the situation. Option B is a trait theory.

questions.question: The political scientist who, in 1978, first distinguished 'transforming' leadership from 'transactional' leadership was:
questions.explanation: James MacGregor Burns introduced the contrast between transforming and transactional leadership in his 1978 book Leadership, and Bernard Bass later developed it in 1985. Option B is linked to the contingency model, option A to the followership model, and option D to the Managerial Grid.

questions.question: A factory supervisor tells workers that anyone who misses the day's quota will be issued a query and may lose part of their N80,000 monthly allowance. Which base of power is the supervisor relying on?
questions.explanation: Coercive power comes from the ability to punish or impose penalties, such as queries and pay deductions. Option B comes from followers' admiration of the leader, and option D from the leader's knowledge or skill. Option A is the ability to give benefits, which is the opposite of a threatened deduction.

questions.question: In Fiedler's model, relationship-oriented leaders tend to perform best when the situation is:

options.b: Either very favourable or very unfavourable

questions.explanation: Fiedler found that relationship-oriented leaders do best in situations of moderate favourableness, while task-oriented leaders do best when the situation is either very favourable or very unfavourable. Options C, A and B describe where task-oriented leaders do best.

questions.question: The view that leaders are born, not made, is known as the:
questions.explanation: The Great Man Hypothesis holds that people are born with the qualities that make them leaders, and it is the foundation of the trait approach to leadership. Options A and B tie a leader's effectiveness to the situation and to clearing paths to goals, while Option C suggests behaviour is learned by watching others, so none of them claims leaders are simply born.

questions.question: Under trait theory, height, strength, vigour and appearance are grouped as:
questions.explanation: Height, strength, vigour and appearance are bodily features, so trait theory groups them as physical traits. Option D covers things like interpersonal skills and adaptiveness, Option A covers the ability to comprehend, plan and think, and Option C covers initiative and administrative ability.

questions.question: In trait theory, the ability to comprehend, conceptualise, plan and think belongs to which group of traits?
questions.explanation: Comprehending, conceptualising, planning and thinking are mental capacities, which trait theory classes as intelligence traits. Option A refers to features such as height and vigour, Option D refers to initiative and administrative ability, and Option C refers to qualities such as interpersonal skills and aggressiveness.

questions.question: Initiative and administrative ability are classified in trait theory as:
questions.explanation: Initiative and administrative ability relate to getting a job started and running it well, so they are task-related abilities. Option B is about comprehending and planning, Option A is about interpersonal style and temperament, and Option D refers to bodily features like height and strength.

questions.question: Interpersonal skills, aggressiveness and adaptiveness are examples of which group of leadership traits?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal skills, aggressiveness and adaptiveness describe a person's temperament and way of relating to others, so trait theory lists them as personality traits. Option A covers initiative and administrative ability, Option D covers the ability to think and plan, and Option B covers features such as height and appearance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the groups of traits identified by trait theory?

options.a: Social-class traits such as family name and inheritance
options.c: Intelligence traits such as the ability to plan and think
options.d: Physical traits such as height and vigour

questions.explanation: Trait theory groups leadership qualities into physical traits, intelligence traits, task-related abilities and personality traits, and social class is not one of these groups. Options D, C and B each name a real trait group with a correct example.

questions.question: Which pairing of a trait and its trait group is CORRECT?
questions.explanation: Initiative sits with administrative ability under task-related abilities, so this pairing is correct. Option C is wrong because vigour is a physical trait, Option B is wrong because planning is an intelligence trait, and Option A is wrong because aggressiveness is a personality trait.

questions.question: A managing director led a Lagos distribution firm very well during stable years, but with exactly the same personal qualities he struggled badly when a sudden currency crisis hit the firm. Which limitation of trait theory does this case illustrate?

options.a: It provides no basis for comparing the traits
options.c: It focuses too much on followers' needs
options.d: It assumes leadership is learned through training

questions.explanation: The leader's traits did not change, yet his success did, because the situation changed; trait theory is criticised for ignoring such situational factors. Option A is the other limitation of trait theory, but it concerns measuring one leader's traits against another's, which is not the issue here. Options D and C are not features of trait theory at all, since it holds that leaders are born and it centres on the leader rather than followers.

questions.question: Two consultants assess the same pair of managers for 'vigour' and 'initiative' but cannot agree on any yardstick for saying that one manager has more of a trait than the other. Which limitation of trait theory does this reflect?

options.b: It treats leadership style as fixed by the organisation's policies
options.c: It relies on rewards and punishments to explain leadership
options.d: It provides no basis for comparing the traits

questions.explanation: Trait theory lists qualities leaders should have but offers no basis for comparing those traits between people, which is exactly the consultants' problem. Option A is a real limitation too, but it is about the setting in which a leader works, not about measuring traits. Option C describes transactional ideas and Option B describes bureaucratic leadership, neither of which is a criticism of trait theory.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of trait theory?

options.b: It has not produced an agreed list of leadership traits
options.c: It assumes anyone can become a leader through training
options.d: It provides no basis for comparing the traits

questions.explanation: Trait theory rests on the Great Man Hypothesis that leaders are born, not made, so it does not claim that anyone can be trained into leadership; that statement is the opposite of the theory, not a limitation of it. Options A, D and B are genuine weaknesses: the theory overlooks the situation, offers no yardstick for comparing traits, and has never settled on one agreed list.

questions.question: A leader's ability to influence others that comes from personal sources such as intelligence, wealth or even physical beauty is best described as:
questions.explanation: Power is the capacity to influence others, and it can come from personal attributes such as intelligence, wealth or even beauty. Option A is different because it is the right to command, conferred by culture, society or an organisation. Option D is passing tasks to others and Option C is being answerable for one's actions.

questions.question: In leadership, authority is best defined as:

options.b: The freedom of subordinates to set their own goals
options.c: The ability to influence others through wealth or beauty
options.d: The duty to report to shareholders on performance

questions.explanation: Authority is the right to command, and it is conferred on a person by culture, society or an organisation. Option C describes where power comes from rather than authority, Option D describes accountability, and Option B describes the autonomy given under laissez-faire leadership.

questions.question: Within a company, formal authority is conferred on leaders through:
questions.explanation: In an organisation, the right to command flows from the board of directors, which confers authority on executives and managers. Option C represents workers' interests, Option B buys the firm's products and Option D examines its financial statements, but none of them grants managers the right to command.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a quality that authority should have?

options.a: It should be consistent with individual belief and organisational purpose
options.c: It should be known only to the leader and kept from subordinates
options.d: It should be feasible and capable of being carried out

questions.explanation: Authority must be clear, feasible, consistent with individual belief and organisational purpose, and capable of being carried out; authority that subordinates cannot see is the opposite of clear. Options B, D and A are all qualities sound authority should have.

questions.question: A new branch manager in Ibadan is told by head office to 'handle staff matters as necessary', but nobody explains which decisions she may take on leave, discipline or hiring. Which quality of authority is missing?
questions.explanation: Authority must be clear, so the holder knows exactly what she is allowed to decide; a vague instruction with no stated limits fails this test. Nothing suggests the authority is impossible to exercise, as Option D would mean, or that it conflicts with the firm's purpose or her personal beliefs, as Options A and C would mean.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes power from authority?

options.a: Power and authority mean exactly the same thing and can be used interchangeably
options.b: Power is the right to command conferred by the board, while authority arises from personal beauty or wealth
options.c: Authority comes only from personal wealth, while power comes only from written job descriptions
options.d: Authority is the right to command conferred by culture, society or an organisation, while power can arise from personal sources such as intelligence or wealth

questions.explanation: Authority is a right to command that is conferred, for example by an organisation through its board, whereas power is the ability to influence and can come from personal attributes such as intelligence, wealth or beauty. Option B swaps the two ideas, Option A wrongly treats them as identical, and Option C gets the origin of each one wrong.

questions.question: Under the behavioural theory of leadership, which of the following describes an autocratic leader?

options.a: Sets no goals and lets things drift
options.b: Puts followers' needs and growth first
options.c: Leads by coercion and acts as a fault-finder rather than a coach
options.d: Trusts subordinates and expects their feedback

questions.explanation: The autocratic leader allows no subordinate participation, leads by coercion and looks for faults instead of coaching people. Option D describes the democratic leader, Option A describes the laissez-faire leader, and Option B describes servant leadership.

questions.question: Which pairing of leader type and communication pattern is CORRECT?

options.a: Autocratic leader - two-way communication; democratic leader - one-way communication
options.b: Autocratic and democratic leaders both use only one-way communication
options.c: Laissez-faire leader - one-way communication; democratic leader - no communication
options.d: Autocratic leader - one-way communication; democratic leader - two-way communication

questions.explanation: The autocratic leader passes instructions down with one-way communication, while the democratic leader uses two-way communication and expects feedback from subordinates. Option A reverses the two styles, Option B ignores the feedback the democratic leader seeks, and Option C misdescribes both styles.

questions.question: The main merit of the autocratic leadership style is that:

options.a: Creativity and personal initiative are boosted
options.c: Subordinates take part in every decision

questions.explanation: Because the autocratic leader decides alone without waiting for input, things get done quickly. Option B is the merit of democratic leadership, Option A is the merit of laissez-faire leadership, and Option C is the opposite of autocratic leadership, which allows no subordinate participation.

questions.question: At a Kano packaging factory, the manager decides everything alone, gives orders without explanation and publicly criticises any mistake. Orders are executed fast, but staff are increasingly unhappy and withdrawn. Which drawback of this leadership style is shown?

options.c: It encourages too much entrepreneurial freedom
options.d: It leaves the group without direction

questions.explanation: This is autocratic leadership, whose demerit is that it hurts workers' morale even though work gets done quickly. Option A is the demerit of democratic leadership, while Options D and C relate to laissez-faire leadership, where the leader is absent and gives no direction.

questions.question: A major demerit of the democratic leadership style is:

options.c: Absence of direction from the leader

questions.explanation: Democratic leaders involve subordinates and seek their feedback before deciding, which takes time and makes decision-making slow. Options A and C are demerits of the autocratic and laissez-faire styles respectively, and Option B is a feature of the autocratic leader.

questions.question: Which of the following is a merit of the laissez-faire leadership style?

options.a: It ensures strict compliance with policies
options.b: It gets things done quickly through firm control
options.c: It provides close direction at every stage
options.d: It boosts creativity and personal initiative

questions.explanation: Because the laissez-faire leader sets no directives and lets individuals think and decide for themselves, the style boosts creativity, personal initiative and an entrepreneurial mindset. Option B is the merit of autocratic leadership, Option C is the opposite of a style in which the leader is largely absent, and Option A describes bureaucratic leadership.

questions.question: At a start-up in Yaba, the founder rarely shows up, sets no targets and lets each team do as it likes. Some new ideas emerge, but projects wander off course and deadlines are missed. Which demerit of laissez-faire leadership is shown?

options.a: Decisions are slow because everyone must be consulted
options.b: Rigid rules block every new idea
options.c: The leader is not there to give direction, so the group easily drifts
options.d: Workers' morale is hurt by coercion

questions.explanation: Laissez-faire leaders are often absent and give no direction, so the group easily drifts, which is exactly what is happening here. Option A is the demerit of democratic leadership, Option D is the demerit of autocratic leadership, and Option B describes an over-bureaucratic setting rather than one with no rules.

questions.question: Which pairing of leadership style and its demerit is CORRECT?

options.c: Autocratic - easy for the group to drift

questions.explanation: Democratic leadership involves subordinates in decisions, so its demerit is slow decision-making. Option C is wrong because drifting is a laissez-faire problem, Option B is wrong because coercion belongs to the autocratic style, and Option D is wrong because autocratic leadership gets things done quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a quality of an effective leader?

options.a: Keeping away from subordinates to protect one's authority

questions.explanation: Effective leaders are decisive, have a vision, are empathetic with good conceptual skills, and have interpersonal skill, all of which involve engaging with people rather than avoiding them. Options D, B and C are each listed qualities of an effective leader.

questions.question: Faced with two competing proposals and a tight deadline, the head of a Lagos logistics firm weighs the facts and makes a firm choice the same afternoon instead of postponing. Which quality of an effective leader is she showing?
questions.explanation: Making a firm, timely choice between alternatives rather than putting it off is decisiveness, which is a key quality of an effective leader. Option D is about understanding others' feelings and Option C is about relating well with people, while Option A is a physical trait, and none of these describes making the decision itself.

questions.question: A mental picture of what someone aims to achieve within a time frame, given the constraints they face, is called a:
questions.explanation: A vision is the mental picture of the future a person or organisation aims to reach within a time frame, given its constraints, and goals and objectives then make it more concrete. Options B and C are guidelines and step-by-step methods for doing things, and Option D is a financial plan, so none of them is the broad picture of what is to be achieved.

questions.question: Which option arranges vision, goal and objective from the broadest to the most concrete?
questions.explanation: A vision is the broad mental picture, a goal narrows it down, and an objective is more concrete than a goal. For example, quality education is the vision, university education is the goal, and a four-year course is the objective. Option D reverses the order, while Options B and A put the middle and last items in the wrong places.

questions.question: Tunde's aim in life is a quality education. To achieve it, he decides to obtain a university education, and he enrols for a four-year degree course. In this example, the four-year degree course is his:
questions.explanation: The four-year course is the most concrete, specific target, so it is the objective. Option A is the broad aim of a quality education and Option D is the university education that narrows it down. Option B is not one of the three levels in this example.

questions.question: Which of the following is a role of a leader?

options.b: Leaving subordinates to settle every conflict on their own
options.d: Keeping key information away from followers

questions.explanation: A leader is expected to be firm and decisive in decisions and to bring people together towards the group's goal. Options B and D would divide the group rather than unite it, and Option C is the opposite of being firm and decisive.

questions.question: The sales and finance departments of an Abuja firm have been feuding for months. The new MD meets both teams, settles their differences and gets them working on a joint plan. Which role of a leader is the MD performing?

options.a: Enforcing rules as a compliance officer
options.d: Being firm and decisive in decisions

questions.explanation: Uniting feuding groups and getting them to work towards a shared plan is the leader's role of bringing people together. Option D is the other role of a leader, but the case is about reconciling people rather than making a firm choice, Option B is a physical trait, and Option A describes bureaucratic leadership.

questions.question: Relationship-oriented leadership places greatest emphasis on ____
questions.explanation: Relationship-oriented leaders focus on the people side of work: supporting followers, building trust and caring about their well-being. Options B, C and D all describe task-oriented behaviour, where the emphasis is on monitoring, supervising and controlling the work itself.

questions.question: Leadership behaviour that focuses on structuring tasks and clarifying roles reflects ____
questions.explanation: Task-oriented leaders concentrate on getting the work done by organising tasks, setting standards and making roles clear. Relationship-oriented leadership (C) focuses on people and support instead, while visionary (B) and servant leadership (D) emphasise future direction and serving followers.

questions.question: Leadership influence that shapes organisational norms is referred to as ____
questions.explanation: Leadership that shapes the shared norms, values and habits of an organisation is called cultural leadership. Technical leadership (B) is about expertise in tasks, coercive leadership (C) relies on threats, and transactional leadership (D) is about exchanging rewards for performance, not shaping norms.

questions.question: Transformational leadership focuses on inspiring followers by emphasising ____
questions.explanation: Transformational leaders inspire followers by appealing to shared values and a compelling vision, encouraging them to go beyond self-interest. Extrinsic rewards (B) are the tool of transactional leaders, while strict procedures (A) and routine compliance (C) fit bureaucratic styles.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four dimensions of transformational leadership?
